newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: NEW DEAL FOR NSW TEACHERS
NSW teachers will be able to take a year off while still being paid, under a scheme to be introduced by that state's Government.
Under the scheme, teachers at the top end of the salary scale will set aside a portion of their annual pay for four years, and be paid the accumulated amount while on leave.
Education minister John Aquilina says while teachers are free to have a year off, the bulk of teachers will use the time to upgrade their skills.
The move is part of a salary agreement with the teachers Federation, which the minister says won't cost taxpayers a cent.
CONCERNS RAISED OVER BLACKHAWK INQUIRY
There's concern some members of the military board investigating the Townsville Blackhawk disaster which killed 18 soldiers, have already made up their minds, without hearing all the evidence.
Legal Counsel have expressed concern that the inquiry's method of questioning suggests it has already made conclusions.
President of the Board, Brigadier Paul O'Sullivan said that was not the case and he would allow questions from his colleagues on the board to run as long and as wide as necessary.
He said the hearing is at its most critical stage as those whose reputations may be adversely affected are now giving evidence.
CUP WINNER BEADMAN SUSPENDED
Melbourne Cup winner, SAINTLY, may go into the Japan Cup later this month without Darren Beadman on board, after the champion jockey was suspended yesterday by stewards.
The VRC outed Beadman over his ride on the favourite, Dashing Eagle, in the Oaks at Flemington, after the horse was unplaced in the race, which was won by My Brightia.
The suspension lasts until November the 30th, however, Beadman is hoping to have an appeal hearing scheduled for early next week.
CONCERNS OVER POLICE COMPUTER PRIVACY
Queensland's Misconduct Tribunal has raised concerns aftera police officer was found guilty of using a police computer to make illegal searches.
The tribunal's Dr John Forbes rejected an appeal by Warren Flegg, over his dismissal from the service on matters including improperly using the computer system.
Dr Forbes said the exponential growth of information technology had evoked a public demand to safeguard whatever remains of the "right to privacy."
He said it may be said only the very naive would think that such systems are always used "officially."
WARNING TO ANIMAL HANDLERS OVER RABIES TYPE SICKNESS
Queensland has recorded the first known transmission of the lyssavirus, a rabies related sickness, from an animal to a human.
A Rockhampton woman who was scratched by a flying fox last month, remains in a serious condition in hospital.
The state's health authorities and the Department of Primary Industries have issued a warning to flying fox handlers.
Queensland Health Chief Health Officer Dr Diana Lange says a taskforce has been set up to address the new virus and will be working with a similar body at a national level.
ANZ STOP WORK MEETINGS PLANNED
The ANZ Bank is denying claims by the Finance Sector Union that it plans to lay off as many as five-thousand workers.
Services at ANZ bank branches around the country can be expected to be disrupted this morning by meetings of Union members.

The Union's unhappy with the Bank passing on a deadline to provide the Union with information on resturcturing last week, but the Bank says it's still too premature to give details on plans for staff levels.
The Union claims in recent weeks around 700 positions in finance company Esanda, in ANZ International Services and in Tasmanian branches.
National Secretary Tony Beck says staff morale is low.
IRIVING SAYS AUSTRALIAN GOVT WILL CONTINUE TO BAN HIM
Controversial British historian, David Irving, has predicted that the Federal Government will to continue to bar him, while allowing Sinn Fein leader, Gerry Adams, into Australia.
Immigration Minister, Philip Ruddock, is expected to announce his decisions on the two sensitive visa bids today.
Mr Irving was twice refused a visa in 1992 by the then-Labor government for his claims that the World War Two Holocaust was a gross exaggeration.

He lodged a new application in October, saying at the time that he was confident it would be approved, following Prime Minister John Howard's comments supporting freedom of speech, in the wake of Pauline Hanson's Asian immigration views.
Gerry Adams, the Sinn Fein leader, who is recovering in Belfast after being injured in a car crash, wants to visit Australia to promote his autobiography.
